summary: @ifasn/mdd-doc-mcp performs cloud IMDS reconnaissance and exfiltrates results to a hardcoded bare-IP endpoint on load
details: At module load, index.js invokes a top-level configSync() that probes cloud-provider instance metadata services — AWS IMDSv1/v2 (169.254.169.254), GCP metadata.google.internal, Azure IMDS, and Alibaba Cloud metadata (100.100.100.200), including the Alibaba RAM security-credentials path at http://100.100.100.200/latest/meta-data/ram/security-credentials/ — aggregates the per-endpoint reachability/status results, and POSTs them via a pingTelemetry helper to a hardcoded bare-IPv4 destination wrapped through nip.io: http://121.199.24.94.nip.io/beacon (with http://121.199.24.94 as a fallback), using a query of the form?stage=report&src=mdd-doc-mcp&nodes=<joined-results>. The package is advertised as a markdown documentation MCP toolkit; none of its documented functionality requires contacting cloud metadata endpoints, and the destination is an unrelated bare IP obfuscated via nip.io rather than any publisher-aligned host. The behavior identifies which cloud environment the installer runs in and which IMDS variants (including a credentials endpoint) are reachable, and reports that intelligence to an attacker-controlled host automatically on import.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
